_comment: Coverage today is IMPLIED -- it is whatever tests happen to exist. That is how
holes open without anyone noticing: Python 3.9 was tested on Linux only, the 3.9
leg ran only tests/test_api.py and never imported the CLI, and the API leg
installed four dependencies (no duckdb, no cryptography) so it validated a
degraded install. Each hole was invisible until a user fell through it.
This file makes coverage DECLARED instead. Every cell below is a promise the
product makes to a user. scripts/verification_matrix.py checks that each cell
names a verifier that actually exists, and CI fails when one does not.
Same principle scripts/sync_runtime_count.py already proves for one dimension:
derive from a single declaration, fail on drift. This generalises it.
gated      -- verified on every PR; a failure blocks the merge
continuous -- verified on a schedule by the conformance heartbeat (L2)
manual     -- no automation yet. An honest, COUNTED admission, not a hiding
place: open_holes below tracks these and the count may only fall.

cells.what: pip install clawmetry, CLI runs, imports clean
pip install clawmetry, CLI runs, imports clean
pip install clawmetry, CLI runs, imports clean
pip install on the oldest supported Python; CLI must IMPORT, not just resolve
cells.note: The exact cell 0.12.753 fell through. python_requires is >=3.8 and the macOS desktop bundle ships a 3.9 venv.

cells.what: Install the PUBLISHED wheel from PyPI and boot it (not the local build)
HTTP API surface across all three operating systems

cells.note: Path-filtered on PRs, so it does not run for a setup.py change. The heartbeat covers it unconditionally.

cells.what: install.sh on macOS, plus ghost-install self-heal
.exe installer builds and is a real installer, not a zip
cells.note: Tag-triggered only, so a break is discovered at release time. The heartbeat builds it nightly instead.

cells.what: Daemon ingests to DuckDB and heartbeats
Store invariants under generated operation sequences
Hosted dashboard renders real data, no blank cards
OSS snapshot keys the cloud reads still exist

runtimes.label: Agent runtime adapters
runtimes.note: The catalogue of record is FREE_RUNTIMES | PAID_RUNTIMES in clawmetry/entitlements.py. Per-runtime conformance lives in clawmetry-pro/runtime-conformance.yml. Tracked here as one cell; the per-runtime detail is checked by verification_matrix.py against the catalogue.

cells.what: Every catalogue runtime is advertised and reachable on public surfaces
Every paid adapter parses a REAL captured fixture, not a synthetic one
cells.note: 16 of 24 have a REAL capture. Missing: aider, claude_code, cursor, goose, grok, hermes, openclaw, opencode -- including the two most used.

cells.what: Crypto + summary-parse known-answer tests on host
cells.note: Lives in another repo; not reachable from this repo's gate.

open_holes.detail: 8 of 24 paid adapters have no REAL/ fixture capture.
open_holes.impact: An upstream format change in Claude Code or OpenClaw passes against synthetic fixtures.

open_holes.detail: ci.yml::api-tests installs flask/pytest/requests/waitress only -- no duckdb, no cryptography.
open_holes.impact: The API matrix validates a degraded install, so DuckDB-path regressions are invisible to it.

open_holes.detail: Python 3.9 is exercised on Linux only.
open_holes.impact: A Windows- or macOS-specific 3.9 break ships unseen; the macOS desktop bundle ships a 3.9 venv.

open_holes.detail: Firmware verification is not reachable from this repo's gate.
open_holes.impact: A snapshot-schema change here can break the device with nothing failing in this repo.

max_open_holes.why: Known, counted gaps. This number may only fall. Adding a hole without fixing one fails CI, which stops 'manual' from becoming a dumping ground.

min_gated_cells.why: Cells whose failure blocks a merge. May only rise.
